title: Symmetry-Twisted Multi-Entropies: Order Parameters for 2D SPT Phases
authors: Ramanjit Sohal, Michael Levin, Ruben Verresen
abstract: Although symmetry-protected topological phases (SPTs) can be distinguished by their entanglement properties, it has been unclear how to extract this information directly from expectation values beyond the 1D case. Here, we close this gap and propose a pair of nonlocal order parameters that can detect and distinguish all bosonic SPTs in 2D protected by internal discrete, Abelian unitary symmetries. The desired topological invariants are extracted by these quantities by effectively simulating the SPT path integral on topologically non-trivial spacetime manifolds. Our order parameters are defined in terms of expectation values of partial symmetry and permutation operations acting on fixed numbers of replicas of the system in finite spatial regions. These expectation values correspond to symmetry-twisted versions of multipartite entanglement quantities known as multi-entropies. We show explicitly that our two order parameters detect symmetry-protected four-party and six-party entanglement, respectively, and we constrain possible "spurious" contributions. We analytically test our proposal in fixed-point lattice models. Our results suggest multipartite entanglement to be a defining feature of SPTs; indeed, we expect our methods to generalize to fermionic and higher-dimensional systems.
summary: The paper introduces symmetry-twisted multi-entropies as nonlocal order parameters capable of classifying 2D Symmetry-Protected Topological (SPT) phases. By analyzing expectation values involving multiple system replicas and partial symmetries, the authors derive specific quantities whose quantized phases encode the topological invariants associated with these phases. This provides a robust theoretical tool to probe entanglement structure beyond simple bipartite measures.
main_problem: To develop nonlocal order parameters capable of detecting and distinguishing all bosonic Symmetry-Protected Topological (SPT) phases in two dimensions, overcoming limitations associated with local correlators.
main_result: The authors propose symmetry-twisted multi-entropies ($\Lambda_r^g$ and $\Omega_{g,h,k}$) that serve as order parameters whose quantized phases specify the topological invariants classifying 2D Abelian SPTs based on braiding statistics.
method: The method involves defining these order parameters using expectation values of partial symmetry and permutation operations acting on multiple replicas of the system state in finite spatial regions.
model_or_system: The focus is on bosonic SPT phases in two dimensions protected by internal discrete, Abelian unitary symmetries ($G = \prod_i \mathbb{Z}_{N_i}$). The analysis uses wavefunction expectation values rather than explicit flux insertion into the Hamiltonian.
key_observables: Nonlocal order parameters $\Lambda_r^g(\psi)$ and $\Omega_{g,h,k}(\psi)$, whose quantized phases ($\vartheta$) correspond to topological invariants (Type-I, II, and III SPT classes).
important_parameters: The symmetry group $G$, the number of replicas ($R$), and the structure of the Abelian symmetries.
main_assumptions: The method assumes that these multi-entropy quantities effectively simulate the path integral on topologically non-trivial manifolds, allowing extraction of topological invariants purely from wavefunction expectation values.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the replica structures and partial symmetry actions for the proposed order parameters ($\Lambda_r^g$ and $\Omega_{g,h,k}$), showing how they are constructed using multiple copies of the system state.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first identifying the need for nonlocal probes (Chunk 1). It then formalizes the general multi-entropy structure using replica techniques (Chunk 2). The core mathematical development involves calculating and simplifying the phase factors ($	ilde{\Omega}_{g,h,k}$) associated with plaquette boundaries on a lattice (Chunks 3 & 4), culminating in identifying this factor as a TQFT partition function.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, purely entanglement-based diagnostic tool for characterizing topological order, which is highly relevant to understanding exotic phases of matter studied in AMO physics and condensed matter theory.
